title: Protocol for real-time imaging, polar protein quantification, and targeted laser ablation of regenerating shoot progenitors in Arabidopsis
protocol: Cut out 0.25 cm–0.5 cm of green portions using pre-sterilized and cooled Vanna’s micro-scissors within the LAF.
Place the excised portion at the center of a 35 mm sterile petri-dish containing 3 mL of solid SIM medium within the LAF.
Cool down a drop of 0.75%–0.8% molten agar to approximately 37°C and place it next to the sample.
Using a sterile micro-tip, drag the droplet towards the sample and let it seal the sample from all sides.
Wipe the working area, the stage, and the controller of the microscope with 70% ethanol.
Turn on the power of the laser-scanning confocal microscopy system.
Initialize through the integrated imaging software.
Add 5 ml of 20 μg/mL PI stain to the SIM containing a 35 mm petri-dish.
Allow the sample to stain for 20 min before draining it out.
Place the 35 mm petri-dish with the sample onto the universal mounting frame.
Orient the petri-dish to ensure that the arrow on its side aligns with the edge of the left slider of the universal mounting frame.
Go to the “Acquisition Interface”.
Click on “Show All Tools” located at the top of the “Acquisition” interface.
Under “Setup Manager”, choose lasers “Argon and DPSS 561” and turn them ON.
Click on the dropdown menu for “Imaging Set Up”.
Click on “Channels” and choose to switch track every “Frame”.
Choose the sensitive channel “Ch2m” for GFP and “Ch3” for chlorophyll autofluorescence from “Track 1”.
Keep emission range of 488 laser at 490 nm–510 nm for GFP (green pseudo-color).
Keep emission range of 650–750 nm for chlorophyll autofluorescence (blue pseudo-color).
Choose the Main Beam Splitter “488/561”.
Click on “Add a new track”.
Choose the sensitive channel “Ch2m” for GFP and “Ch3” for chlorophyll autofluorescence.
Set emission range of 514 laser at 525 nm–550 nm for YFP (magenta pseudo-color) and 650–700 nm for chlorophyll autofluorescence (blue pseudo-color).
Choose the Main Beam Splitter “458/514/594”.
Click on “Add a new track”.
Choose the sensitive channel “Ch2m” for PI stain.
Set emission range of 561 laser at 580 nm–610 nm for PI stain.
Go to “Acquisition Parameter” and select “Acquisition Mode”.
Click on “Objective” and choose 10 × objective.
Focus the sample under the 10× objective.
Adjust the digital “zoom” to 0.6 from “Scan Area”.
Check “Track 1” and “Track 3” under “Channels”.
Proceed to check excitation lasers 488 and 561 respectively.
Set the laser power for 488 nm and 561 nm to 50.
Set Gain (Master) for Ch2m, Ch3, and T-PMT in Track 1 to 750, 650, and 170 respectively.
Set Digital Gain to 1 for all four channels in Track 1.
Check “Track 2” and proceed to check excitation laser 514 nm.
Set the laser power for 514 nm to 50.
Set Gain (Master) for Ch2m, Ch3, and T-PMT in Track 2 to 750, 650, and 170 respectively.
Set Digital Gain to 1 for all three channels in Track 2.
Adjust the pinhole to 1 Airy Unit by clicking on “1AU”.
Uncheck all Tracks except Track 1.
Go to “Experiment Manager” and click “Live”.
Scan for progenitors tagged with pPIN1::gPIN1-GFP.
Use the stage control joystick or other stage movement control to scan through the sample visually.
Once progenitors are spotted, set the work position for the stage by selecting the “set work position” option from the controller.
Set the work position carefully without touching the sample.
Go to "Acquisition Mode" on the software, select "Averaging", and set "Number" to 1.
Bring progenitors to the center of the imaging frame using the stage control joystick.
Go to "Acquisition Mode", select "Frame Size", and set it to 512 × 512.
Capture an image at scan speed 6 for location reference.
Label the progenitors in the captured images as L1, L2, etc.
Carefully bring the stage down without disturbing the petri-dish.
Pipette 5 mL of filter-sterilized PI into the petri-dish.
Optional: Pipette 5 mL of autoclaved Milli-Q water instead of PI if cell boundary visualization is not required.
Wipe the lens and ceramic collar of the 40× water-dipping objective with methanol before imaging.
Go to "Acquisition Parameter".
Select "Objective" and choose 40 × water-dipping objective.
Bring the stage back up using fast auto focus.
Use fine adjustment to focus the sample under 40× magnification.
Center the progenitor in the frame using the stage control joystick.

Adjust imaging parameters: laser power at 50%, pinhole up to 3 Airy Scan Units (AU) if needed, Gain (Master) between 650–700, digital offset at 1, frame size at 1024 × 1024, digital zoom at 0.6, scan speed at 5, and line averaging at 2.
Adjust the Gain (Master) just below fluorescence saturation based on progenitor brightness.
Go to “Experiment Manager”, check the “Z-stack” option.
Fast scan z-position with Track 1 until progenitor cells are out of focus, then click "Set first".
Focus through the sample in the opposite direction until progenitor cells are once again out of focus and click "Set last".
Repeat using Track 2.
Set the interval (step size) to 1 μm in the “Z-stack” pop-up window for polarity quantifications.
Set the interval (step size) to 5 μm in the “Z-stack” pop-up window for time lapse imaging across multiple intervals.
Capture the image from the “Acquisition” interface.
Click on “Start Experiment” from “Experiment Manager”.
Ensure all three tracks are turned on before starting the experiment.
Work fast during parameter setting and image capture to prevent sample overstaining.
Do not expose the sample to laser for long periods to avoid de-localizing PIN1-GFP from the membrane.
Save captured z-stack images as .czi format.
Reconstruct Z-stacks into a projection view with Zeiss LSM software.
Drain PI (or Milli-Q water if sample was unstained) using a pipette.
Take out the petri-dish and wash the fixed sample with 5 ml of autoclaved Milli-Q water 2–3 times.
Seal the petri-dish with PhytaWrap and return it to the growth chamber.
Wash the sample by pipetting Milli-Q water gently along the sides of the 35 mm petri-dish, ensuring not to dislodge the sample.
Repeat steps from 3a-3v every 24 hours (or as frequently as needed).
Ensure that the imaging parameters remain identical for one progenitor throughout the time course.
Open the first image of the time lapse series for a progenitor and go to “Dimensions” in the software.
Click on “Reuse” to apply the same settings as those described for the first-image of the time lapse series.
Place the petri-dish on the microscope stage in the same orientation each time.
Use the image captured under 10× magnification for finer adjustment of orientation and as a terrain map for reference.
Capture the image with 40× water dipping objective while keeping the sample submerged in Milli-Q water to avoid overstaining the sample during imaging.
Add 5 mL of 20 μg/mL PI stain to the SIM containing 35 mm petri-dish.
Allow the sample to stain for 30 minutes.
Place the petri-dish on the universal mounting frame, aligning the arrow with the left slider edge.
Follow the instructions from the previous section until step 3.o of "Imaging of the sample".
Carefully lower the stage without moving the petri-dish.
Pipette 5 mL of autoclaved Milli-Q water into the dish.
Continue to follow the instructions from step 3.p to 3.v of "Imaging of the sample".
Work quickly to set parameters and capture images under a 40× objective with Milli-Q water.
Quantify the pixel intensity of PIN1-GFP along the plasma membrane using Fiji/ImageJ software.
Define regions on the plasma membrane for each selected cell.
Measure the pixel intensity for each defined region.
Extract the positions of each selection on the plasma membrane.
Plot a graph of pixel intensity against the exact position on the plasma membrane.
Identify the side of the cell with the highest peak of signal intensity to determine PIN1-GFP polarity.
Acquire a z-stack image of a progenitor with 1 μm step size in .czi format or .lsm format.
Open the acquired image using Zen Image processing software.
Mark the boundary of the cells with a membrane reporter such as PI.
Ensure all sides of the selected cell are conspicuous and free from interference by overlaying or underlying cells.
Go to “Processing” in the software.
Click on “Copy” from the drop-down option under “Method”.
Choose “Subset” from the drop-down options.
Go to “Method Parameters”.
Click on the “Select” option corresponding to the file name of your input image.
This will display all the X, Y and Z coordinates of the input image.
Choose z-positions that span only through the cell you want to quantify using the slider or up/down arrow buttons.
Adjust “Start” and “End” under “Z” in “Method Parameters” to the chosen z-positions.
Click on “Apply”.
Convert the subset image into TIFF format.
Go to “File” and choose “Export” from the drop-down options.
Choose “Tagged Image File Format” from the pop-up window’s drop-down options.
Click “Select File Name and Save”.
Open the TIFF image in ImageJ/Fiji software.
Select one cell of the progenitor with cell membrane-localized PIN1-GFP and PI.
Go to "Image" option in the Fiji window toolbar, select "Color", and click on "Split Channel".
Zoom into the image to focus on a single cell for polarity quantification.
Draw a boundary over the cell membrane using the Freehand Selections tool in the PI channel window.
Go to “Analyse” and choose “Set Measurements”.
Check ‘Centroid’ option from the window.
Go to “Analyse” option in the tool bar and select “Measure”.
Note down the centroid coordinates provided in the “Results” window.
Close the channel for PI (blue) and the results window.
Select the channel for PIN1-GFP (green).
Select the “Brush Tool” from the toolbar.
Mark the centroid of the cell using the centroid coordinates with the brush tool.
Choose a color to mark this point, e.g., white.
Mark another point exactly above the centroid using the “Brush Tool”.
Ensure that the X-axis value is the same as that of the centroid.
Choose a different color other than white, for instance red, to mark the point above the centroid.
Select the “Multipoint Tool” from the tool bar.
Use the multipoint tool to mark multiple points along the PIN1-GFP marked cell membrane.
Space the points as close as possible.
Choose a different color, for instance yellow, for marking multiple points.
Prepare a working solution for injection 30 minutes before each time point.
Set up measurement parameters to quantify PIN1-GFP signal corresponding to each multipoint on the membrane by going to "Analyze" and clicking on "Set Measurements".
Select "Mean Gray value" from the pop-up window and click "OK".
Measure the PIN1-GFP signal corresponding to each multipoint on the membrane.
Copy all measurement data from the "Result" window into a new Excel sheet.
Open the previously saved snapshot of the cell marked with multipoints in Fiji/ImageJ.
Select the “Angle Tool” from the toolbar.
Click on the red dot, white dot (centroid), and yellow dot (first measurement point) in sequence using the cursor.
Measure the angle between the three dots by going to "Analyze" and clicking on "Measure".
Repeat step 5.v for each subsequent measurement point.
Copy the calculated angle values to an excel sheet.
Ensure the angle value corresponds to the previously measured Gray Value for the same point.
Define the red dot as 0˚/360˚ angle.
Calculate angles from the positive Y axis in a clockwise direction.
Plot a graph using Mean Gray Value of PIN1-GFP against 0°- 360˚ angle.
Trace back points to determine the side of the cell with the highest PIN1-GFP localization intensity.
Repeat steps 5.c to 5.y to quantify the polar localization of PIN1-GFP in other cells of the progenitor.
Acquire a z-stack image of a progenitor with a 1 μm step size in .czi or .lsm format.
Open ZEN2.3 SP1 Black Edition software.
Open the z-stack image of the progenitor for which polarity needs to be quantified.
Process raw images sequentially using Zen software steps (1–4) to create maximum intensity projections.
Map the localization pattern of PIN1-GFP based on the qualitative measurement of its signal intensity.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Follow steps 3a-3v from the time-lapse imaging protocol to capture a pre-ablation z-stack image using a 40× water dipping objective.
Deselect all tracks except for "Track 1" corresponding to GFP under "Channels" in acquisition parameters for locating progenitor cells.
Go to “Dimensions” and click “Crop” to zoom into the center of the target cell such that the cell fills the entire frame.
Use the “zoom” option under “Scan Area” to adjust the view if needed.
Minimize laser exposure time by working quickly during digital zoom at 35-40.
Go to “Acquisition Parameter”, and choose “Channels” for locating non-progenitor cells.
Under “Channels”, deselect all tracks except for “Track 2” (corresponding to YFP).
Click on “Live” to quick scan through the progenitors to choose the target cell.
Go to “Setup Manager” on the “Acquisition” interface and turn ON the laser “405”.
From “Track 4”, check the channel corresponding to “Ch1” detector.
Go to “Dye” corresponding to “ch1” detector, click on the drop-down menu provided and select “DAPI”.
Keep the remaining two channels (Ch2m and Ch3) in Track 4 unchecked.
Go to “Range” corresponding to “ch1” detector, and keep the emission range at 409 nm–465 nm.
Choose the “Main Beam Splitter” (MBS) “405”.
Go to “Acquisition parameters” and check only Track 4 (DAPI).
Go to “Lasers”, then check the box corresponding to “405 nm”.
Increase the laser power of 405 nm to 80%.
Set pinhole to 1AU.
Set Gain (Master) for Ch1 to 800.
Start a timer for 30 seconds.
Go to “Experiment Manager” and click on “Continuous” to activate continuous scanning.
Stop scanning immediately after 30 seconds, then give an interval of 30 seconds.
Follow up with another 30 seconds of continuous scan.
Choose an easily accessible cell, preferably one which is on the surface.
Start with two pulses of 30 seconds each, separated by a resting interval of 30 seconds.
Fine-tune ablation time based on cell type and age (troubleshooting available).
Post ablation imaging to study regeneration.
If ablation was done on GFP expressing progenitor cells, go to “Acquisition Parameter” and choose “Channels”.
Uncheck Track 4 to inactivate the laser 405.
Check the box corresponding to Track 1 to turn it ON.
Go to “Acquisition Mode” under “Acquisition Parameters”.
Decrease the “Zoom” to 1.2 by using the slider or typing in “1.2.”
Increase the Gain (Master) to 800 and fast scan the field of view by clicking on “Live”.
Open the pre-ablation image captured.
Go to “Dimensions” and click on “Reuse”.
Set the “Set First” and “Set Last” of the z-stack.
Go to “Experiment Manager” and click on “Start Experiment” to capture the post ablation z-stack image.
Save the post-ablation image as .czi format or .lsm format.
Repeat the laser ablation steps if remnants of fluorescent cells or additional cell bodies are present.
Inspect the T-PMT channel image to confirm cellular damage.
Drain the PI/Milli-Q water using a pipette after bringing down the stage.
Wash the sample with autoclaved Milli-Q water 2–3 times.
Seal the petri-dish with PhytaWrap and return it to the growth chamber for further imaging.
Capture a time-series of post-ablation images following steps 3.a to 3.v of “Imaging of the sample” protocol.
Ensure the time interval between each image is not more than 5 hours.
If ablation was done on non-progenitor cells, go to “Acquisition Parameters”, choose “Channels”.
Uncheck Track 4 (corresponding to DAPI) to inactivate laser 405 used for ablation.
Check the box corresponding to Track 2 (corresponding to YFP) to turn it ON.
Repeat steps 10.a.iv to 10.a.xii.
Note: The fluorescent puncta seen at the site of ablation is autofluorescence from debris of ablated cells.
The debris clears within 48 hours, after which it no longer fluoresces.
